text:
Sam: quick heads-up — ran a perf sweep on the mixed-quant pipeline (FP8 primary, INT8 fallback, 4-bit experiments) against the longctx prefill workload. Seeing weird TTFT spikes on prefill but decode TPS improves. dumping profiler now, any ideas?

Maya: share the numbers + profiler snippet please.

Sam: pasted raw numbers — baseline (no quant) prefill p50 ~120ms, now ~170ms (+42%). decode p50 ~35ms -> still ~35ms but decode TPS changed from 28 -> 33. Prefill tail got worse.

Sam: profiler hotpaths:
```
quant_router.cpp:route_kernel 38%
kvcache::write_batch 22%
prefill_scheduler.cpp:dispatch 18%
kernel_selector.cpp:compile_or_reuse 12%
memcopy: 6%
```

Jin: looks like routing/compile churn — when kvcache contents change between microbatches we flip quant routes and trigger kernel selection. that costs a lot in prefill because many KV writes and quant conversions happen up front.

Maya: +1. prefill touches full KV write set per request; decode often reuses cached KV so routing is cheaper. two quick levers: (1) add hysteresis to quant routing to avoid flip-flopping (e.g. quant_routing_hysteresis_ms), (2) avoid INT8 fallback on prefill path so kernel path is stable.

Jin: proposing experiment commands:
```
# run perf harness w/ hysteresis
rperf run --model redwood/gptq-fp8 --workload longctx-prefill --config quant_routing_hysteresis_ms=200 --out /tmp/runs/hyst

# run w/ prefill-only fallback disabled
rperf run --model redwood/gptq-fp8 --workload longctx-prefill --config prefill_quant_fallback=none --out /tmp/runs/no_fallback
```

Sam: ran both quick. hysteresis reduced kernel switches by ~80% and brought prefill p50 to ~135ms, still above baseline. disabling prefill fallback = p50 ~128ms. decode TPS delta: hysteresis -> 31, no-fallback -> 30. microbatch merging changed TPS a lot.

Maya: interesting — so hysteresis helps latency but decode TPS slightly lower vs the +33 earlier. probably because hysteresis delays switching to a faster decode kernel when safe. tradeoffs.

Sam: I also observed heavy KV eviction at microbatch boundaries: KV eviction spikes correlate with kernel churn. snippet from flamegraph: kvcache::evict spikes at same timestamps as kernel_selector activity.

Jin: that implies two interacting heuristics: our microbatch merger tries to reduce p99 by merging small requests, but it can also cause KVs to be flushed/merged incorrectly causing routing differences. try batch_hysteresis_ms and batch_merge_token_threshold params.

Sam: ran microbatch tweak: batch_merge_token_threshold=24 + hysteresis=200ms. results: decode TPS up to 36, prefill p50 ~132ms, but single-request tail rose for tiny requests.

Maya: that's acceptable for the canary target (we optimize throughput for bursty traffic). action items: (a) implement quant_routing_hysteresis with per-path tuning (prefill stricter), (b) add prefill-only disable_fallback flag, (c) add a perf CI job that runs longctx-prefill & decode with FP8/INT8/4bit combos.

Jin: I'll prototype the config knobs and add telemetry: counters for kernel_switches, kvcache_evictions, and route_decisions per-request. also add a small synthetic that toggles KVs mid-prefill to reproduce.

Sam: SGTM. I've captured the rperf outputs and uploaded to /shared/perf/171234-prefill-quant. attaching a short CSV with raw TTFT/TPS.

ops-bot: deploy-bot started canary: quant-routing-hysteresis V2 -> eng-runtime-canary.

Maya: thanks — let's watch the canary for p50/p95 prefill and kernel_switch count. if p50 > 150ms we rollback.

Sam: noted. will post dashboard links and the CI job PR once Jin has prototyped. :eyes: :thumbsup:
